title.narrative: Global Observatory of Teacher policies and Global Report on Teacher 2026: Generating, managing and disseminating knowledge on Teachers through the 2nd Global Report on Teachers and the TTF Knowledge Platform

description.narrative:
This project focuses on Knowledge Management and Production key elements of the Main Line of Action 1 of the current 2022-25 Strategic Plan (SP) of the Teacher Task Force (TTF). Its expected results and key achievement will contribute to the current and the upcoming Strategic Plan of the TTF.
The first ever Global Report on Teachers, coauthored by the TTF and UNESCO and generously funded by the Hamdan Foundation, was launched in February 2024 at the Policy Dialogue Forum in Johannesburg, South Africa in February 2023. The event attracted more than 300 key education stakeholders from all over the world and over 300 online views. More than 300 copies were distributed on-site, with ample press coverage in Spanish, English, and French. Since its launch, the report has been consulted 7,610 times on the UNESCO digital library, viewed 2,200 times on the TTF Knowledge Hub, and downloaded 1,427 times. It has also been presented at numerous local, regional, and global events; notably the Global Gateway High-Level Education Event (Brussels), the AFTRA Conference (Zambia), and the G20 Education Working Group Meeting (Brazil). Plans for launching the forthcoming Chinese, Spanish, Portuguese, and Arabic editions through partnerships with TTF members are expected to significantly increase its outreach.
The second edition of the Global Report on Teachers, scheduled for spring 2026, will continue to address pressing global issues affecting teachers and the teaching profession. Building on the previous report covering teacher shortages, examining their various dimensions and how to mitigate the factors leading to them, the 2026 report will cover a specific thematic issue to be agreed upon by the Teacher Task Force Steering Committee and UNESCO, relevant to the achievement of the SDG4.c, but it will not deal with monitoring progress towards its achievements. Using country data, new commissioned research and good practices, it will provide analysis and issue recommendations for the final years towards achieving the 2030 Agenda and the Target 4.c.
The proposed thematic direction of this second edition will be discussed and validated through consultations with the TTF Secretariat, UNESCO TED section, and the upcoming TTF Editorial Board. To ensure its global relevance, the Global Report on Teachers 2026 will also seek alignment with key international platforms reshaping global education strategies and initiatives, including follow-up actions from the Transforming Education Summit and the Recommendations of the High-Level Panel on the Teaching Profession, alongside critical topics to be addressed during the Summit of the Future (2024) and the Summit for Social Development (2025).
Alongside knowledge production, the TTF also undertakes knowledge monitoring and dissemination to ensure that relevant and up-to-date knowledge on teachers and teaching is available to inform the formulation and implementation of comprehensive teacher policies. Since 2020, the TTF Knowledge Platform is a flagship activity within these efforts.
To fulfil its monitoring function, the platform currently comprises two knowledge repositories: the Policy Knowledge Hub and the Teacher Resource Centre. The Policy Knowledge Hub (having grown to more than 600 curated pieces by 2024) hosts reports, academic research, grey literature and other documents that help inform effective policy-making. Launched in 2023, the Teacher Resource Centre responds to the identified need to collect and disseminate resources for teachers, teacher educators and trainers themselves to support effective teaching.
Beyond its monitoring function, the Knowledge Platform has proved to be a catalyser of policy learning, by providing permanent access to the body of knowledge generated by regional and thematic communities of practice. The number of national policy documents and related materials hosted in the repository substantially increased during the regional workshops in 2022 and 2023. Policy learning is further supported through technical materials hosted in the Teacher Resource Centre, such as teacher training modules to support the development of teacher competencies in line with stated policy objectives. As revealed by a user survey conducted in 2022, the support to policy learning was one of the platform’s most valued features. Building on this, the next phase in the development of the Knowledge Platform will focus on further tailoring the content of the repositories and the navigation functionalities to meet TTF policy learning needs.
